history.period: 1501 CE (restored 1681 by Ramdev Manikya; 20th century by Radha Kishore Manikya)
history.summary: CSV TOWN CORRECTION: this shrine is NOT at Amarpur — it stands at Matabari (Matarbari) on the south-western outskirts of Udaipur town, Gomati district, ~55-60 km from Agartala; the state of Tripura is named after it. CSV 'state' column wrongly held the town name — corrected to Tripura. OVERLAP: an existing dataset file 'tripureshwari-temple-matabari-udaipur' (1026.json) already covers this same temple — keep-or-merge decision needed. The temple is one of the 51 Shakti Peethas (legend: the right foot / Dakshin Charan of Sati, including the big toe, fell here); the goddess sits on a turtle-shaped hillock (Kurmaprishthakriti), considered the holiest site for a Shakti shrine, also called Kurma Pitha. The main shrine, a cubical edifice with a three-tier roof, was erected in 1501 by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya in the Bengali Ek-ratna style; the Kalyan Sagar lake lies beside it. The sanctum holds two black-stone idols: the 5-ft Tripura Sundari and the 2-ft Chhoto-Ma (Chandi), the latter said to have been carried by Tripura kings to battle and hunts; rituals are maintained by descendants of priests invited from Kannauj. Redeveloped under the Union Tourism Ministry's PRASHAD scheme (Rs 52 crore + Rs 7 crore state) and inaugurated by the Prime Minister on 22 September 2025; a 51-Shakti Peethas Park is under construction 4 km away at Banduar.

name: Tripureswari Temple
town_description: Udaipur is the former capital of princely Tripura and headquarters of Gomati district, about 55 km from Agartala on the Gomati river. Known as a 'lake-town' for its historic royal lakes, it is Tripura's foremost temple town, home to the Tripura Sundari Shakti Peetha at Matabari and several other old Manikya-era temples.
